title: Prophecy Against Mount Seir (Edom)

questions.question: Against what specific mountain region is Ezekiel told to prophesy in chapter 35?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:2 (ESV): "Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it,"

questions.question: Who inhabited Mount Seir?
questions.explanation: Mount Seir is the mountainous territory encompassing Edom, inherited by Esau (Genesis 36:8).

questions.question: What does God say He will make Mount Seir?
options: A fortress for the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:3 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you, and I will make you a desolation and a waste."

questions.question: Why is judgment coming upon Mount Seir (Edom)?
options: Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity
Because you worshipped the golden calf
Because you stole the ark of the covenant
Because you made an alliance with Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:5 (ESV): "Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment,"

questions.question: God says, "Since you did not hate bloodshed, therefore... "
options: you shall be drowned in the sea
the sword will depart from your house
you shall live in the desert without water
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:6 (ESV): "therefore, as I live, declares the Lord God, I will prepare you for blood, and blood shall pursue you; because you did not hate bloodshed, therefore blood shall pursue you."

questions.question: What will God do to the traveler who crosses over Mount Seir?
options: He will cut off from it all who come and go
He will demand a tribute from him
questions.correctAnswer: He will cut off from it all who come and go
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:7 (ESV): "I will make Mount Seir a waste and a desolation, and I will cut off from it all who come and go."

questions.question: What greedy ambition of Edom is quoted in verse 10, bringing God's anger?
options: "These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them"
"We will conquer Babylon and sit on its throne"
"We will take all the gold from the temple of Solomon"
"We will rule the Mediterranean Sea alone"
questions.correctAnswer: "These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:10 (ESV): "Because you said, 'These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will take possession of them'—although the Lord was there—"

questions.question: What was Edom ignoring when they claimed the two nations (Israel and Judah) would be theirs?
options: That Babylon was still too strong

questions.question: How does God say He will deal with Edom for their anger and envy against Israel?
options: "I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your enmity against them."
"I will forgive you seventy times seven times."
"I will ignore your boasts because Israel was wicked."
"I will send fire from heaven without warning."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your enmity against them."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:11 (ESV): "therefore, as I live, declares the Lord God, I will deal with you according to the anger and envy that you showed because of your enmity against them..."

questions.question: Edom spoke abusively against the mountains of Israel, saying, "They are laid desolate; they are given us..."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:12 (ESV): "when you said, 'They are laid desolate; they are given us to devour.'"

questions.question: With what did Edom magnify themselves against God, multiplying their words against Him?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:13 (ESV): "And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth, and multiplied your words against me; I heard it."

questions.question: When the whole earth rejoices, what will God make of Mount Seir?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:14 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate."

questions.question: Edom rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate. So what will God do to Edom in return?
options: "I will deal with you in the same way; you shall be desolate, O Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it."
"I will bless Edom to show Israel the depth of my mercy."
"I will send the rain to Edom but not to Israel."
"I will force Israel to serve Edom forever."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will deal with you in the same way; you shall be desolate, O Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:15 (ESV): "As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so I will deal with you; you shall be desolate, O Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it."

questions.question: The judgment on Edom repeats the main theme of Ezekiel regarding the recognition of God. What is it?
options: "Then they will know that I am the Lord."
"Then they will know that judgment is near."
"Then they will repent in dust and ashes."
questions.correctAnswer: "Then they will know that I am the Lord."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 35:15 (ESV): "Then they will know that I am the Lord."

questions.question: What relationship did Edom (descendants of Esau) originally have with Israel (descendants of Jacob)?
options: They had never met until the exile
They were masters and slaves in Egypt
They were both given the land of Canaan equally
questions.explanation: Esau and Jacob were twin brothers. The enmity of Edom was considered worse because it was against a brother nation. Thus "perpetual enmity" (v. 5) is highlighted.

key_verse_text: "Because you cherished perpetual enmity and gave over the people of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of their final punishment,"
